answer: Establishment requires cosigners, and cosigning is convex. Keys with overlapping funding share one island, and a new key enters the grading set only with guarantees from three keys on a different island from its own. A guarantor's k-th open guarantee locks k squared units, so backing 30 keys locks 9,455. Each epoch the beacon names a falcon, an auditor key that re-grades a random sample; when a guaranteed key is caught, every guarantor's locked sum is slashed into the ocean, the pool paying honest graders. An honest newcomer costs its backers 1 unit each; 100 clones put 94,550 at risk.
